senses.d: The study of the physical properties of the earth, including how humans affect and are affected by them.
ex: Some amount of basic geography is part of any good curriculum for primary and secondary education.

senses.d: An atlas or gazetteer.
A description of the earth: a treatise or textbook on geography.
Terrain: the physical properties of a region of the earth.
Any subject considered in terms of its physical distribution.
Similar books, studies, or regions concerning other planets.
The physical arrangement of any place, particularly (UK, slang) a house.
The lavatory: a room used for urination and defecation.
ex: The Business Man Jocular: ‘I say, where's the geography, old son?’

senses.d: The relative arrangement of the parts of anything.
ex: The actual geography of the murderous mind is still a mystery.

senses.d: A territory: a geographical area as a field of business or market sector.
ex: We currently operate only in EU countries but we're building prototype services for various geographies.

senses.d: The branch of mathematics dealing with spatial relationships.
A mathematical system that deals with spatial relationships and that is built on a particular set of axioms; a subbranch of geometry which deals with such a system or systems.
ex:
1975 [Addison-Wesley], Eugene F. Krause, Taxicab Geometry, 1986, Dover, page 64,
Entire new geometries are also suggested by real-world cities.

senses.d: The observed or specified spatial attributes of an object, etc.
ex: The inset of figure 1 shows the geometry of the samples. They are 4.6 mm long and 0.4 mm wide.
Also, certain SCSI controllers need to be told where to find drive geometry in order for Linux to recognize the layout of your drive.

senses.d: A mathematical object comprising representations of a space and of its spatial relationships.

ex: The architect used geometric techniques to design her home.

ex: Bacteria exhibit geometric increase in numbers when the environment is not limiting.
